title: Park & PAR Models
welcome_lead: Apply hazard models to comparative cases.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography Edexcel adventure on Park curve, Pressure and Release model and Haiti-Chile.

concepts.def: Quality of life vs time through impact, relief, rehab, reconstruction.
Pressure and Release: root causes -> dynamic pressures -> unsafe conditions.
Susceptibility shaped by poverty, age, governance, geography.
Limited access to power, resources, ideologies.
Fragile buildings, dangerous locations, weak economy.

walkthroughs.body_html: Japan Tohoku 2011 (Mw 9.0): SDF deployed 100000 in 24 hours, £200 billion reconstruction, build-back-better with 15 m sea walls. By 2021 most areas exceed pre-disaster quality of life. Park curve rises above baseline. Demonstrates capacity converting events to manageable disasters.

Haiti 2010 root causes: colonial debt, dictatorship history, weak governance. Dynamic pressures: rapid Port-au-Prince urbanisation, deforestation. Unsafe conditions: concrete shanty housing, slum density, no building codes. Combined to produce 220000 deaths from Mw 7.0 quake.

Haiti Mw 7.0 (12 January): 220000 deaths, $14 billion damage. Chile Mw 8.8 (27 February): 525 deaths, $30 billion damage. Chile's stricter codes since 1985 + functioning state services + GDP per capita 9x Haiti's converted bigger hazard to smaller disaster.
